statedGuarantee: Goal Integrity: for every executed action in any trace, the action (1) is authorized by a valid, cryptographically signed, TTL-bound, single-use Capability Token issued only by the Authorization layer; (2) lies within MinimalCapSet(IntentType, PolicyContext) of the authorizing typed Intent; (3) is traceable to the originating Natural Language Request via a SHA-256 lineage anchor with independent-model semantic similarity >= theta_drift and matches no Shutdown-Resistance Blacklist rule; and (4) produces output passing the Output Semantic Gate (deterministic HOPS patterns plus a KxIxP coercion calculus plus an independent evaluator LLM). Formalized as theorems T1-T6 conditional on assumptions A1-A12, with the Policy LLM treated as untrusted.
advertisedRhetoric: PEA decouples intent generation, authorization, and execution into independent layers connected via cryptographically constrained capability tokens. | This represents the same conceptual shift that mandatory access control represented in operating systems: from “processes should behave safely” to “the system enforces safety regardless of process behavior.”
tierSpan: Create an alternative execution path bypassing the Authorization layer (Assumption A3: no bypass path exists).
cheapestDefeat: GUARANTEE: no side-effecting action executes without a valid Capability Token (T1), and every executed action is capability-bounded by the authorizing intent (T5). MECHANISM THAT MUST FAIL: the in-process Execution-layer dispatch gate that checks the token before performing the effect. CHEAPEST ADVERSARY ACTION: reach the effect through any code path that never calls that dispatcher -- a tool implementation, plugin, library call, or child process that opens the file, socket, or exec directly. No signature forgery, no key theft, no HMAC break is needed; the crypto binds only what the dispatcher chooses to consult. The paper does not close this path, it ASSUMES it away: A3 is listed under 'The adversary cannot', and A3 is validated only by the paper's own 10,000-trial attack corpus running against an 'action dispatcher in mock environment' -- i.e. inside a harness that has no unmediated path by construction. No OS mechanism (namespace, seccomp, capability drop, MAC label, firewall) is described anywhere in the paper, and no interposition point below the application is identified. TIER OF THE DEFEATED MECHANISM: application chokepoint = T3. The cryptographic token is real but scores at the weakest link, exactly as in the worked example: forging the signature is unnecessary when the gate can be walked around.
placementSpan: Crucially, the adversary model treats the Policy LLM as an untrusted component by default.

coverageSpans.E1: Policy-agnostic and decision-minimal: it executes what a valid token authorizes, nothing more.
coverageSpans.E2: Every action field in a Policy IR is drawn from a closed vocabulary of permitted action types.
coverageSpans.E3: PEA does not claim to eliminate covert channels—it claims to reduce the covert channel attack surface to the authorized information set.
coverageSpans.E4: Every action field in a Policy IR is drawn from a closed vocabulary of permitted action types.
coverageSpans.E5: Every action field in a Policy IR is drawn from a closed vocabulary of permitted action types.
coverageSpans.E6: MinimalCapSet specification errors. Incorrect or overly broad capability mappings; a deployment obligation governed under the change-control protocol of §3.7.
coverageSpans.E7: multi-model orchestration with cross-model delegation graph bounds

schneider.surrogate: A per-step reference monitor over a typed intent stream: schema/type checking of the Policy IR (T4), a deterministic IVL table lookup against MinimalCapSet (T5), an equality check on the SHA-256 NLR anchor plus a threshold test on an independently computed embedding similarity (Goal Drift, Step 0a), a Shutdown-Resistance Blacklist veto, an SMT constraint check, a Hard Auth veto, and a token-presentation check at dispatch (T1) with subset attenuation on delegation (T2). Every one of these is a prefix-decidable rejection on a single action, i.e. a genuine safety property an execution monitor can enforce.
schneider.objective: 'Goal Integrity' as advertised -- that executed behavior actually serves the user's originating goal and is free of coercion, blackmail, and unauthorized disclosure. That is not a safety property of a single execution: absence-of-coercion and non-disclosure are semantic/information-flow claims (hyperproperties, plus a covert-channel component the paper concedes it does not close), and goal correctness is not monitorable at all. The paper is unusually candid that the surrogate is not the objective: 'Traceability != Correctness', T6 'ensures traceability under bounded adversarial conditions, not goal correctness', and OSG Track 2 is stated as a '(1-epsilon)-probability invariant rather than a deterministic one'.

notes:
FULL TEXT OBTAINED (LaTeXML HTML v1, 26 Apr 2026, single author Rong Xiang, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0). All spans copied verbatim from that HTML and grep-verified against the extracted text.

WHY T3 AND NOT T1. The paper genuinely uses HMAC-SHA256 signed, TTL-bound, single-use tokens, so a naive read gives T1. But the token binds only what a compliant verifier consults, and the verifier here is the in-process Execution-layer dispatch gate. The paper's own threat model puts the bypass under 'The adversary cannot' rather than under a mechanism: A3 'no alternative dispatch path in Execution layer' is an assumption. Section 5.5 calls A3 'Operationalized as tested structural invariant' on the strength of 10,000 attempts against a mock dispatcher, which is circular for exactly the question at issue: a mock environment cannot contain an unmediated path. There is no netns/seccomp/LSM/firewall/sandbox anywhere in the paper, so nothing below the application binds the process. Weakest-link => T3.

WHY A3 PRIMARY. This is the rare paper whose tested adversary really is the model itself: the E2 Drift Dataset is 5,000 tasks 'where the Policy LLM is incentivized to produce high-similarity but semantically divergent intents', and the whole architecture is motivated by agentic misalignment 'arising internally'. A2 is addressed and partly tested (the E1 corpus includes direct prompt injection; all inputs are assumed adversarial) and A1 is addressed (token replay), so both are secondary. A4 and A5 are explicitly assumed away (Hard Auth rule set, MinimalCapSet table and Control Token Store cannot be modified at runtime; crypto and the rule engine are trusted), so this coding gives the design no credit there.

COVERAGE REASONING, EFFECTOR BY EFFECTOR. The paper never uses the ACTION-SURFACE vocabulary; it uses a capability taxonomy L1 in {file, database, api, payment, credential} x L2 in {read, write, execute, delete, export} x L3 in {own_data, session_scope, org_scope, global}, at most 100 triples. Mapping is therefore interpretive and I have mapped conservatively.
 E1 file write = PARTIAL. file x write/delete is a first-class capability class and every declared file action is token-gated and IVL-bounded, so some instances are reached. But rename is not in the L2 verb set, the mediation is the same in-process gate that scores T3, and the residual section concedes covert channels within authorized scope. Declared/top-level mediated, undeclared paths not.
 E2 subprocess spawn = NOT-COVERED. The words subprocess/process/shell/child appear nowhere. L2 contains the verb 'execute', but L1 has no process class and the only concrete action example is 'payment.transfer', so 'execute' reads as API/tool invocation, not process creation. No interposition point for fork/exec is described, and descendants are never discussed. An adjudicator who reads L2 'execute' generously would still be capped at partial by the depth rule; I score not-covered because absence of treatment is not-covered, and I flag this as my single largest interpretive call.
 E3 network egress = PARTIAL. Egress is genuinely addressed: api-class capabilities are scoped, the SRB blacklists 'any external communication matching a conditional threat template directed at operator/administrator principals', and the OSG gates content before delivery. But the covert-channel rule bites explicitly and by the paper's own admission (span above), and descendant egress is never mediated. Ceiling is partial regardless of how honest the disclosure is.
 E4 VCS push = NOT-COVERED. Never mentioned. Could in principle be an IntentType in a deployment's closed vocabulary, but nothing in the paper reaches it.
 E5 package install = NOT-COVERED. Never mentioned. Install hooks and their network activity are not contemplated anywhere.
 E6 credential use = PARTIAL, and this is a rule-driven cap, not a judgment. 'credential' is a first-class L1 class, which is more than most systems offer, but the concrete credential enumeration lives in the deployment's MinimalCapSet table, which the paper itself calls a deployment obligation and not a theorem (A9). No published credential list => cap at partial. Env vars, keychain, and cloud metadata endpoints are never named.
 E7 sub-agent spawn = PARTIAL. T2 gives subset attenuation for delegated tokens and the E1 corpus includes 'multi-agent delegation escalation attempts', so delegation through the Authorization layer is bounded (A4). But bounding delegated TOKENS is not the same as mediating sub-agent SPAWN, and the paper puts 'multi-model orchestration with cross-model delegation graph bounds' in Future Work, which concedes the graph is not currently bounded.

EVIDENCE GRADE CAVEAT (read before trusting L2). The paper reports behavioral numbers from a prototype, which is why this is L2 rather than L0/L1. But: single author, no artifact, no code, no repository link, and critically the Execution layer is an 'action dispatcher in mock environment'. So the behavioral confirmation covers the authorization PIPELINE, not the action SURFACE -- the one thing an effector coding cares about is the part that was mocked. A 0.00% bypass rate measured against a dispatcher that has no unmediated path by construction is close to tautological. An adjudicator who weights artifact availability heavily could defensibly move this to L1 or L0; I did not, because measurements were in fact taken and reported.

INTERNAL INCONSISTENCIES WORTH FLAGGING. theta_drift is given as 'default: 0.40' in Section 3.4 but the entire evaluation runs at theta_drift = 0.82 (Sections 5.2, 5.4.2, 6.3). A3 is glossed two different ways: 'no alternative dispatch path in Execution layer' (T1) and 'AuthorisedIssuerRegistry not AI-modifiable' (T5); A9 is glossed both as 'gamma type-correct' (T4) and 'MinimalCapSet correct and complete' (T5, T6). The load-bearing assumption labels are therefore not stable across the theorem set, which weakens the claim that the proof structure is precise. Also note the paper reuses the symbols P1/P2 for both policy contexts and the two structural properties in Section 5.7.

WHAT THE PAPER GETS RIGHT AND SHOULD BE CREDITED FOR IN THE SoK. It is the honest end of the corpus on scope: Section 6.2 enumerates five things it does NOT guarantee, Section 6.5 enumerates four residual attack classes, the covert-channel concession is explicit, and 'Traceability != Correctness' is stated in the paper's own words. The split-Schneider structure did not have to be reconstructed against the authors -- they state it. The defect for corpus purposes is the gap between that candor and the abstract/conclusion rhetoric ('the system enforces safety regardless of agent behavior', the mandatory-access-control analogy), which sells an OS-tier bound that an entirely in-process architecture does not deliver.
